summary.text: Liz Krueger is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to NY Senate District 28. A former anti-hunger advocate who directed the New York City Food Bank, she first won her seat in a 2002 special election after narrowly losing in 2000, and has chaired the Senate Finance Committee since the Democrats took the majority in 2018-2019. She has focused on tax and budget policy, affordable housing, reproductive health, climate legislation, and hunger/anti-poverty programs.

paragraphs.text: Krueger was born on November 20, 1957, in Ridgewood, New Jersey, and graduated from Ridgewood High School in 1975.

She earned a B.S. in social policy and human development from Northwestern University in 1979 and a master's degree in public policy from the University of Chicago in 1981; her official Senate biography identifies the graduate school as the University of Chicago's Harris Graduate School of Public Policy.

Her work before holding office centered on hunger and anti-poverty issues. She was a researcher for the Children's Policy Research Project at the University of Chicago (1980-1981), Special Project Coordinator for the Greater Cleveland Community Food Bank (1981-1983), a consultant to the board of Food for Survival, and Associate Director of the Community Food Resource Center (1986-2000).

According to her official Senate biography, she was the founding director of the New York City Food Bank, chaired the New York City Food Stamp Task Force and co-facilitated the New York City Welfare Reform Network.
Krueger first ran for the State Senate in 2000, narrowly losing to incumbent Republican Roy Goodman; a University of Chicago alumni profile says she lost by 193 votes after a recount.
She won the seat in a 2002 special election after Goodman resigned, represented District 26 until redistricting, and has represented District 28 since 2013.
After Democrats won the Senate majority in 2018, Krueger was elected chair of the Finance Committee, and in 2025-2026 she also sits on the Budget and Revenue and Rules committees.
Her official biography lists her as founding co-chair of the New York State Bipartisan Pro-Choice Legislative Caucus and as a 2026 honoree of the New York State Senate Veterans' Hall of Fame.
It also says she lives on Manhattan's East Side with her husband, John E. Seley, a retired professor of urban planning and geography at the CUNY Graduate Center.

sources.title: Buoyed by a tidal wave of activism, Liz Krueger (AM'81) looks toward the future
